title: controlplane-reconcile-delay-resolver-collision
creator: Aisha Park
description: Several dedicated customers reported transient hostname resolution errors after large-scale Dedicated GPU pool rotations. Symptoms: short windows (30s-90s) where tenant-scoped hostnames resolved to an unrelated tenant's endpoint, causing internal routing failures and application-level errors. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and the targeted code change to remove the window that allows resolver-affinity metadata to become stale during control-plane peering reconciliation.
reproduction_steps: Provision a Dedicated cluster with VPC peering enabled and two tenant namespaces (T1, T2)
Configure per-tenant egress resolver affinities and short DNS TTLs (30s) for test names
Trigger a scale event that rotates GPU nodes in the pool (simulate autoscaler drain + recreate)

Observe especially during peering-control-plane reconciliation window: resolver binding metadata for one tenant is temporarily overwritten by a delayed reconciliation batch, then the resolver IP is reused by another tenant's SNAT mapping
Query tenant-scoped hostname; in affected windows response contains CNAME/A records pointing to the wrong tenant
root_cause: A deferred control-plane reconciliation batch path that reconciles peering and resolver-binding metadata on a delayed timer. When node rotation and peering state churn happen concurrently, the reconciler writes resolver-affinity mappings out-of-order. The ephemeral resolver IP is reused by SNAT allocator during the same window, producing a collision where a tenant's hostname resolves to an IP currently attached to a different tenant's egress path.
mitigation: Hotfix: add immediate invalidation of resolver-affinity cache on peering state change and force a reconfirmation RPC to the egress allocator (deployed as runtime-1.22.1-canary)
Temporarily increase DNS TTL floor for affected tenants to 120s (customer-facing mitigation to reduce churn) for high-risk customers who reported outages
Operational: onboard affected customers to a temporary routing-fallback policy (canary to global-resolver pool) while we validate fix
proposed_fix: Change reconciliation to a compare-and-swap update for resolver-affinity records, persist monotonic reconciliation tokens, and introduce a transient lock for resolver-binding during peering handoff. Add end-to-end tests that simulate concurrent autoscaler-driven host rotation + peering resync. The PR implements CAS semantics and explicit invalidation hooks for peering events.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy canary runtime-1.22.1 to 1% Dedicated capacity (currently deployed) and monitor resolver-mismatch alerts and customer error rates
Stage 2: If canary is clean for 48 hours, roll to 25% and increase observability retention and sampling of DNS queries for impacted tenants
Stage 3: Full ramp to 100% with a rapid rollback playbook if we detect recurrence within a 5-minute window
Stage 4: Post-rollout, run a targeted 72-hour validation with affected tenants and keep temporary TTL increase for 48 hours after ramp complete
